hypothesis: The baseline timing-driven net-weight update caps weights at `max_net_weight` and uses the default `net_weighting_scheme`; switching the update to the "lilith" scheme (momentum-based criticality accumulation) via the shown `TimingOpt.update_net_weights` dispatch will spread weight onto more moderately-critical nets, reducing many moderate violations (TNS) rather than only the worst path (WNS).
expected_effect: TNS improves on all three cases (more nets get nonzero weight), WNS roughly neutral to slightly better, overflow unchanged, runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dTNS gains (+9.2% to +22.2%) generally exceeding dWNS gains (+12.4% to +15.4%), consistent with lilith spreading weight to moderately-critical nets and reducing many violations rather than only the worst path. All runs valid, no failures. Next step: sweep the lilith momentum/accumulation parameter and `max_net_weight` cap to confirm the TNS-over-WNS tradeoff is tunable and check overflow stays acceptable (~103–113) at higher weight spread.
